children: Iron ore prices lost ground on Tuesday, dragged down by rising supply from major suppliers and sluggish demand for the key steelmaking ingredient in top consumer China.
The most-traded iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
closed daytime trade down 0.74% at 671 yuan ($100.57) a metric ton.
The benchmark December iron ore (SZZFZ6) on the Singapore Exchange was down 0.81% at $90.5 a ton, as of 0715 GMT.
Supply pressure persisted amid rising shipments and arrivals, analysts at broker Everbright Futures said in a note.
Iron ore shipments from major suppliers Australia and Brazil rose 1.3% from the week before to 27.9 million tons as of November 2, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
Demand, meanwhile, remained subdued in China as steelmakers were cautious about restocking ore due to weak profit margins, softer downstream steel consumption and elevated steel inventories.
and coke (DCJcv1), other steelmaking ingredients, shed 2.53.% and 1.57%, respectively, weighed down by anticipation of increased supply.
A Mysteel survey showed coal mines in northern China's Shanxi province continued to resume operations, with 40 mines remaining shut as of November 2, down from 44 a week before.
Several mines had been closed for safety inspections following a fatal accident in Shanxi in May.

Bearish sentiment dominated the steel market amid seasonally weaker downstream steel demand and an absence of policy support in November, analysts at broker First Futures said in a note.
